# Personas — BackOffice Lead Qualification View

Confirmed during User Stories Planning (2026-07-09): a single persona covers all BackOffice users in this increment (`backoffice-story-generation-plan.md`, Question 1 = A).

## Persona: DMC Sales Staff

**Role**: Internal DMC commercial/sales team member responsible for converting leads generated by the chat agent (`apps/chat`) into enrolled students.

**Context**: Today, this persona has **no dedicated tool** — leads exist only inside `agent-service`'s database, invisible to staff unless someone queries Postgres directly. Every prior increment of this project targeted the lead's own chat experience, never the staff side.

**Goals** (from Question 2's resolved answer — prioritization, tied to speed and staying the human checkpoint):
- Quickly see which leads deserve attention right now, without reading full conversation transcripts or querying the database.
- Triage a growing list of leads across Hot/Warm/Cold tiers to decide who to prioritize.
- Reduce the manual work of writing a personalized first-contact message from scratch for every hot lead — but retain final control over what actually gets sent, since these messages represent DMC to a prospective student.

**Frustrations this view addresses**:
- No visibility into which leads are actually worth acting on today.
- Drafting a good, personalized outreach message for every hot lead by hand doesn't scale as lead volume grows.
- Missing time-sensitive leads because nothing currently alerts staff when one becomes hot.

**Explicitly NOT a goal for this persona in this increment**:
- Editing a lead's score or adding manual notes (FR-5 — the `Lead` record stays read-only; scoring is fully computed by the agent's `score_lead()`/BR-17/BR-17b).
- Fully autonomous outreach — this persona wants to reduce manual drafting effort, not remove themselves from the loop. Every outbound message requires their explicit review and "Send" (FR-12).

**Technical comfort**: Assumed to be a standard business user (comfortable with web apps, not comfortable with databases or code) — this shapes the UI toward a simple, glanceable board rather than a data/admin tool.
